In [[optimization (mathematics)|optimization]], a '''gradient method''' is an [[algorithm]] to solve problems of the form 

:<math>\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\; f(x)</math>

with the search directions defined by the [[gradient]] of the function at the current point.{{clarify|reason=The search direction in the conjugate gradient method cannot be calculated using only the gradient at the current point, so what this sentence means is unclear.|date=August 2026}} Examples of gradient methods are the [[gradient descent]] and the [[conjugate gradient]].
